apiKey.description: Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Every path except /health and /ready requires the key. The server reads the key at startup from the environment variable that the `api_key_env` configuration key names, and it does not start without a key. A request with more than one Authorization header gets 401.

apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
apiKeyHeader.description: The Anthropic client header. /v1/messages and /v1/messages/count_tokens accept it as an alternative to the bearer token. When a request sets x-api-key, the server checks only that header: a wrong or unreadable value, or more than one x-api-key header, gets 401 even when the bearer token is valid.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token is missing or wrong. The code is unauthorized.

BadRequest.description: Code bad_request: the request fails a schema or bounds check, and error.message names the field. A body larger than 16 MiB also gets bad_request. Code context_length_exceeded: the prompt is below the context limit of the engine but larger than its memory pool can hold now. error.message then reads "prompt is too long: N tokens > M maximum", where M is the largest prompt that fits now.

NotFound.description: Code not_found: no engine serves the requested model, no engine has the x-engine id, or the request sets x-session.

CapacityConflict.description: The request does not fit the engine. Code context_limit: the prompt has as many tokens as the context limit of the engine, or more. The server checks this before it queues the job, and error.message reads "prompt is too long: N tokens > M maximum", where M is the context limit minus one. Code memory_plan: the engine cannot reserve the memory that the request needs.

CheckpointFailure.description: Code checkpoint_failure: saved model or cache state failed to load or failed its identity check.

Overloaded.description: Code overloaded: the queue of the engine is full, or the engine is stopped.

BackendFailure.description: Code backend_error: model execution failed, or the engine failed to load or stopped after a native backend failure. The message is always "Model execution failed."

code.description: The failure class. Only GET /ready returns not_ready.

id.description: Model name. Send this value as the model field of a request.

created.description: Unix time in seconds when the server started.

engines.description: Server extension. The engines that serve this model, in the order of the configuration file.

id.description: The engine id from the configuration file. Send it as x-engine to select this engine.

state.description: loading: the engine is starting. ready: it is idle. busy: it is running a job. error: it failed to load. stopped: it has shut down. native-failed: the native backend failed, and the engine takes no more jobs. A request to an engine in state error or native-failed gets 500 backend_error.

model.description: A model name from GET /v1/models. The server sends the request to the first engine that serves this model. x-engine overrides it. A request that sets none of model, x-engine, and x-session gets 400.

temperature.description: 0 selects greedy decoding. The default is the value in generation_config.json of the serving model, else 0.7.

top_p.description: The default is the value in generation_config.json of the serving model, else 1.0.

top_k.description: 0 turns top-k off. The default is the value in generation_config.json of the serving model, else 0.

max_tokens.description: The server lowers it when the prompt plus max_tokens would pass the context limit of the engine.

x-thinking.description: Server extension. Sets the enable_thinking flag of the chat template of the model. default keeps the default of the template.

chat_template_kwargs.description: The thinking switch in the form that vLLM and SGLang accept. enable_thinking true acts as x-thinking on, and false as x-thinking off. Any other key gets 400. An enable_thinking value that disagrees with an x-thinking of on or off gets 400.

stop.description: Stop strings. They match on the decoded text.

x-engine.description: Server extension. The id of the engine to use (see GET /v1/models). When it is set, the server ignores model. An unknown id gets 404.

x-session.description: Reserved. This server keeps no named sessions, so a request that sets x-session gets 404.

strict.description: Accepted but not enforced: the server does not constrain decoding to the parameters schema. It parses tool calls from the model output in all cases.

ResponseFormat.description: Output format. text is the default and applies no constraint. json_object and json_schema get 400 bad_request, because the server has no constrained decoding.

ToolChoice.description: none removes the tools from the prompt. auto, the default, lets the model decide. required and a named function get 400 bad_request, because the server cannot force a tool call.

arguments.description: The arguments as JSON text. A completed call carries a JSON object.

ToolCallDelta.description: One tool call entry in a stream. The server sends each completed call as two entries with the same index. The first carries id, type, function.name, and an empty function.arguments. The second carries the whole function.arguments. A client that joins the arguments strings of one index in stream order gets the full text.

index.description: Position of the call in the message. The first call has index 0.

arguments.description: A fragment of the arguments JSON text.

content.description: A string, or an array of text parts whose text the server joins in order with no separator. Null is valid on an assistant message that carries tool calls.

name.description: A participant name, passed to the chat template. The server ignores a value that is not a string.

reasoning_content.description: The reasoning text of an earlier assistant turn. The server passes it to the chat template of the model, which decides whether to render it. The server ignores a value that is not a string.

tool_call_id.description: Required when role is tool. The value is the id of the assistant tool call that this message answers. The content of a tool message is the result text.

prompt_tokens.description: All prompt tokens, including the ones that a cached prefix served.

total_tokens.description: The sum of prompt_tokens and completion_tokens.

reused_tokens.description: Server extension. Prompt tokens that a cached prefix served, so the engine did not compute them again. It is 0 when a stop string ended the reply before the engine finished the job.

prompt_tokens_details.description: One of the cache usage fields: absent when ENGINESRV_CACHE_USAGE turns them off (see the API description).

content.description: Null when the message has tool calls and no text. It never contains the text of a think block.

reasoning_content.description: Server extension. The text of the think block, without the think tags. Absent when the reply has no think block.

tool_calls.description: Present when the model completed at least one tool call. The server generates the id of each call.

finish_reason.description: stop: end of sequence or a stop string matched. length: the reply reached max_tokens or the context limit of the engine. tool_calls: at least one tool call completed.

created.description: Unix time in seconds when the completion started.

model.description: Name of the model that served the request.

engine.description: Server extension. The id of the engine that served the request.

role.description: The first chunk of a stream carries role assistant. Later chunks omit it.

content.description: Answer text. It never contains the text of a think block.

reasoning_content.description: Server extension. A fragment of the think block text, without the think tags.

tool_calls.description: Tool call entries. A call appears here only after the server has parsed all of it, and completed calls never appear in content. A malformed call, or a call when the request lists no tools, stays in content as raw text.

finish_reason.description: Present on the final chunk only. The values are those of Choice.finish_reason.

created.description: Unix time in seconds when the completion started.

model.description: Name of the model that served the request.

engine.description: Server extension. The id of the engine that served the request.

usage.description: Present on the final chunk only.

id.description: A unique id that starts with msg_.

stop_reason.description: end_turn: end of sequence. stop_sequence: a stop string matched. max_tokens: the reply reached max_tokens or the context limit of the engine. tool_use: at least one tool call completed. Null only in the message_start event of a stream.

stop_sequence.description: The stop string that matched, else null.

signature.description: Always empty. The server does not sign thinking blocks.

input_tokens.description: With the cache usage fields on (the default), the prompt tokens that no cached prefix served, so input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens is the whole prompt. With the fields off, the whole prompt. The message_start event of a stream always reports the whole prompt, because the cached count is known only at the end.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens that a cached prefix served. 0 in message_start, and 0 when a stop string ended the reply before the engine finished the job. Absent when the cache usage fields are off.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Always 0. Absent when the cache usage fields are off.

model.description: A model name from GET /v1/models. The server sends the request to the first engine that serves this model.

max_tokens.description: Required. The server lowers it when the prompt plus max_tokens would pass the context limit of the engine.

system.description: A string, or an array of text blocks. Plain strings are also accepted as array items. It becomes a leading system message. Null counts as omitted.

stop_sequences.description: Stop strings. An empty string gets 400.

temperature.description: Same bounds and defaults as on the chat path.

top_p.description: Same bounds and defaults as on the chat path.

top_k.description: Same bounds and defaults as on the chat path.

stream.description: Selects the Messages event stream. Null counts as omitted.

type.description: enabled and adaptive turn thinking on. disabled turns it off. Without the thinking field, the default of the chat template applies.

budget_tokens.description: Checked to be a positive integer. The server does not limit thinking length by it.

role.description: system is an extension. It adds a system message at its position.

content.description: A string, or an array of blocks. Text blocks join with a blank line. user content takes text, image, document, and tool_result blocks. Each tool_result becomes a tool message in its position; is_error true puts "Error: " before its text. assistant content takes text, thinking, redacted_thinking, and tool_use blocks. Thinking text goes to the chat template of the model as reasoning history, and the template decides whether to render it. The server reads text only: a document with a text source adds its text, and image blocks and other document blocks become short text notes.

input_schema.description: Becomes the function parameters in the chat template.

type.description: auto, the default, lets the model decide. none removes the tools from the prompt. any and tool get 400, because the server cannot force a tool call.

max_tokens.description: Optional. Checked as on /v1/messages (an integer of at least 1), then ignored.

system.description: A string, or an array of text blocks. Plain strings are also accepted as array items. It becomes a leading system message. Null counts as omitted.

stream.description: Checked, then ignored. count_tokens never streams.

type.description: enabled and adaptive turn thinking on. disabled turns it off. The setting can change the rendered prompt and so the count.

input_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the rendered prompt.

200.description: At least one engine is in state ready or busy.

503.description: No engine is in state ready or busy. The code is not_ready, and error.message lists the state of each engine.

200.description: The models of the configured engines, with their engines.

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completion. Set stream to true for server-sent
events. The stream field alone selects the response type; the server
ignores Accept.

Every error before the response headers is a JSON reply with one of
the statuses below, also when stream is true. A streaming response
sends its headers and the first chunk as soon as the engine queue
accepts the job, before the prompt is processed. After that, an
error arrives as one `event: error` in the stream. For example, a
prompt that does not fit the memory pool then arrives as an error
event with code context_length_exceeded, not as a 400.

A client disconnect cancels the job. When a client reads a stream
too slowly and the output buffer of the job fills, the server also
cancels the job. In both cases the stream closes without [DONE] and
without an error event. No request timeout applies.

requestBody.description: The body may be at most 16 MiB. A larger body gets 400 bad_request.

200.description: One completion, or a stream of chunks.

schema.description:
Each event is one data line with a ChatCompletionChunk as JSON, then a blank line:
data: {"id":"...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1700000000,"model":"...","engine":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"..."}}]}
The first chunk carries delta.role assistant and empty content.
Think block text arrives in delta.reasoning_content, never in delta.content.
Each completed tool call arrives in delta.tool_calls as two entries (see ToolCallDelta).
The final chunk has an empty delta, finish_reason, and usage.
A successful stream ends with data: [DONE].
After any 15 seconds without an event, the server sends the comment
line ": keep-alive" and a blank line. Clients ignore comment lines.
An error after the response headers sends one event, for example:
event: error
data: {"error":{"message":"Model execution failed.","code":"backend_error"}}
Its data matches Error, or BackendError for a backend failure. The
server then closes the stream without a final chunk or [DONE].

post.description:
Anthropic-compatible Messages. Authenticate with the bearer token or
the x-api-key header. The model field selects the engine; x-engine is
not available on this path. The server converts the request into a
chat request: system becomes a leading system message, and each
tool_result block becomes a tool message in its position (see
MessageRequestMessage). The server ignores query parameters such as
beta.

With stream true, the reply is the Messages event stream. Every error
before the response headers is a JSON reply, also when streaming. A
client disconnect or an aborted job closes the stream with no error
event and no message_stop.

Context and memory failures get 400 invalid_request_error; this path
has no 409. For a prompt that is too long, error.message reads
"prompt is too long: N tokens > M maximum". A checkpoint failure gets
500 api_error.

requestBody.description: The body may be at most 16 MiB.

200.description: One message, or a stream of events.

schema.description:
Each event is a named SSE event whose data holds one JSON
object. The sequence is message_start, then
content_block_start, content_block_delta, and
content_block_stop for each content block, then
message_delta with the stop reason and the final usage,
then message_stop. The usage of message_start reports the
whole prompt as input_tokens. A failure after the headers
is one error event in the AnthropicError shape, and the
stream ends. After any 15 seconds without an event, the
server sends the comment line ": keep-alive" and a blank
line.

400.description: The request fails a schema or bounds check, or it does not fit the context limit or the memory of the engine. error.type is invalid_request_error.

401.description: The credential is missing or wrong. error.type is authentication_error.

404.description: No engine serves the model. error.type is not_found_error.

413.description: The body is larger than 16 MiB. error.type is request_too_large.

500.description: Model execution failed, or saved state failed to load. error.type is api_error, and error.message is "Model execution failed."

503.description: The queue of the engine is full, or the engine is stopped. error.type is overloaded_error.

post.description: Anthropic-compatible token counting. Authentication, the 16 MiB body cap, and body parsing are the same as on /v1/messages, except that max_tokens is optional and ignored. The server renders the prompt with the chat template of the model and tokenizes it. No engine job runs, and nothing streams.

requestBody.description: The body may be at most 16 MiB.

200.description: The token count of the rendered prompt.

400.description: The request fails a schema or bounds check. error.type is invalid_request_error.

401.description: The credential is missing or wrong. error.type is authentication_error.

404.description: No engine serves the model. error.type is not_found_error.

413.description: The body is larger than 16 MiB. error.type is request_too_large.
